name: Every operator and verifier list change is audited
summary: operators add|remove and verifiers add|remove take --actor OPERATOR and --reason TEXT; restore-new takes both for its re-grants. A real change appends one entry to the runtime-level authority-changes.audit.json beside deployment.private.json (schema_version 1, 0600, 200 entries kept), under the lock and BEFORE the configuration. Every NEW history begins with a compact baseline of the lists as they stood; a list that cannot be read is recorded there as null (UNKNOWN), never as an empty list, and the trail is incomplete for it. An ADD that would start a history while a list cannot be read is refused; a REMOVAL is never refused for the audit or an unreadable list - it records the unknown list as null and goes on. authority-changes prints the trail and the replay; replay.agrees is true, false, or null (no trail yet, or incomplete: one list unreadable now, or null in the baseline); the exit code is 0 either way. A damaged audit never refuses a REMOVAL: the bytes are kept beside it first. The printed placeholders are refused on an ADD and dropped on a REMOVAL (recorded unattributed). NOT covered: a hand edit of deployment.private.json; a list change by an older kit.
